q: What does a large language model actually do when it writes an answer?
exp: It predicts likely text, one token at a time, which is why it can sound right and still be wrong.
o: Predicts the next token again and again, using patterns learned in training
Looks up the answer in a database of checked facts
Searches the internet for every question
Copies a matching sentence from its training data

q: Roughly how many English words are 100 tokens?
exp: A token is often a short word or part of a longer one.

q: Which design, published in 2017, made today's large language models possible?
exp: The transformer looks at every word in a passage at once and works out which ones matter to each other.

q: You want the same, predictable answer every time you sort a message. Which temperature?
exp: Low temperature picks the most likely token nearly every time.

q: Which of these are common problems with generative AI? (Choose all that apply)
exp: Always check facts, numbers and fairness before you rely on an answer.
o: It can never write in plain English

q: A model trained until early this year is asked about yesterday's news. What's most likely?
exp: A model knows nothing after its training finished unless an app gives it current information.
o: It doesn't know, and may make something up if it doesn't say so
It always knows, because models update every night
It refuses all questions about dates
It reads the news on your phone
